A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISM study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DreamBooth personalization and DiffusionDB inversion results, qualitative Wikiart experiments, and component ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional backbone, prompt-length, latency, application, and baseline-comparison results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and all six original system prompts are retained. Appendix C.3 adds limited inference extensions: GPT-4o distillation of generated prompts under a length constraint and composition of independently generated concept prompts.

E1.justification: DreamBooth, Wikiart with PartiPrompts contexts, and DiffusionDB coverage remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds qualitative scenarios involving multiple personalized subjects together and reconstruction from distilled prompts, extending task requirements without adding a benchmark dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds two closely related VLM-based comparators: Liu et al. (2024) in the inversion comparisons, and Idea2Img, adapted to return its selected image's prompt, in DreamBooth personalization. Tables 2, 9, and 10 establish their evaluated participation; the original comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce IDEFICS2 and GPT-4o-mini configurations, 16/32-token controls, a single-stream N=1, K=5 comparison, and latency measurement on an A6000 GPU. Main benchmark splits, metrics, and budgets remain unchanged. Appendix D's new statement that overlong prompts were 'chunked' conflicts with retained clipping instructions, leaving that handling unclear.

E4.justification: v2 adds smaller-backbone and prompt-length analyses, first-iteration versus final judge-score distributions, latency analysis, and composition/distillation case studies. The earlier budget sweeps, stream/iteration trade-off, judge comparison, and re-evaluation ablations are retained and relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without independent-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new judge-score histograms describe distributions across prompts, rather than uncertainty in estimated benchmark performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical and qualitative results. Table 9 reports PRISM/Idea2Img CLIP-I of 0.768/0.759 but NLL of 3.498/2.657, illustrating a metric trade-off. The GPT-4V comparison revises PRISM's inversion NLL/CLIP-I from 2.680/0.777 in v1 Figure 6 to 2.762/0.776 in v2 Table 3. Existing DreamBooth scores and earlier appendix ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The expected judge-score objective and sampling formulation retain their mathematical substance. Score-to-s and sampler notation changes do not introduce new assumptions or reasoning; neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: interpretable, editable, transferable prompts obtained through iterative VLM feedback with black-box T2I access. The added demonstrations and comparisons do not redefine this core claim.

C2.justification: Appendices D–F substantially expand interpretation of readability versus image fidelity, possible compositional failures of VLMs, and financial and latency limitations. They discuss smaller models, reusable prompts, and budget flexibility as practical mitigations. Earlier fidelity, budget-dependence, and CLIP-T limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies IDEFICS2 model variants and their assistant/judge roles, supplies the GPT-4o distillation instruction and comparator adaptation details, and documents latency hardware and API pricing. Existing baseline encoders, history length, re-evaluation details, and full system prompts are retained, often in different locations.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix F substantially expand positioning within LLM-based prompt optimization. They distinguish PRISM from Idea2Img and Liu et al. through reusable prompts, independent streams, judging, and re-evaluation, and add literature on prompt optimization and VLM compositional limitations.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and several explanatory paragraphs, standardizes VLM terminology, moves implementation details and ablation discussions, and separates the ethics statement from the conclusion. The main problem–method–experiments narrative and most existing explanations remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different page format and typography, extensively rearranges figures and tables, converts v1 Figure 6 into Table 3, and adds application, distribution, latency, and comparator displays. Existing budget plots move between the main text and appendices without becoming new results.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1 through close VLM-based comparisons, smaller-backbone and prompt-length controls, and explicit latency and cost evidence. These additions substantially strengthen empirical credibility and assessment of practical applicability. Some superiority wording remains too broad because competing methods achieve lower NLL, and long-prompt handling remains ambiguous, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the added evidence.
